audit.whatIsWrong: Glacial Prison's range is given as 'roughly 900' in two fields, and Abyssal Dive carries no cooldown anywhere.
audit.why: Glacial Prison is 1300. A 400-unit understatement changes where the player stands to open the fight. Abyssal Dive is 21 seconds at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four fields call Thick Skin his 'grey-health passive', one calls Tongue Lash a level-1 stun, three call Frost Armor the 'Permafrost passive', and late calls his ally-save a W.
audit.why: His passive is An Acquired Taste; Thick Skin is the E that banks damage and converts it to a shield on cast. Tongue Lash slows and applies an An Acquired Taste stack — it only stuns a target already carrying three stacks, which cannot be true at level 1. Sejuani's passive is Fury of the North granting Frost Armor; Permafrost is the E stun. The ally-save is Devour, his R.
audit.corrected: Every name corrected to the kit file, and Thick Skin restated as a bankable shield you force out before committing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Frost Armor's slow immunity and Abyssal Dive's knock-up were absent.
audit.why: Frost Armor grants immunity to slows, so Tongue Lash's slow does nothing to an out-of-combat Sejuani — but the An Acquired Taste stack still lands, and a knock-up is displacement, which slow immunity does not touch. That is why Abyssal Dive, not Tongue Lash, is his real opener. The mirror audit reached the same conclusion from his side.
audit.corrected: Slow immunity written into whys[3]; Abyssal Dive's knock-up written into wants.foe[1] as the displacement Frost Armor cannot ignore.

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds timing against a champion who heals off Tongue Lash and banks damage with Thick Skin.
audit.why: Both his Q heal and his E shield sit inside the window your stun chain opens.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal folded into the late-game plan.

edits.after: Tahm Kench's level 1 is almost entirely passive — he takes Q and fishes for Tongue Lash, which only slows and adds an An Acquired Taste stack this early, so stand off his facing angle and deny him the setup. Take W first, hit both strikes whenever he steps up to last-hit, and accept that you are building Frost stacks for a level-2 trade rather than killing anyone. At level 2 you have Q — the moment he walks forward, Q in for the knock-up, land both W strikes for full Frost, and E for the stun; Thick Skin starts banking damage immediately, so end the trade fast and back off before he converts it into a shield.
edits.before: Tahm Kench's level 1 is almost entirely passive — he takes Q and fishes for a tongue lash, so position slightly to the side of his facing angle rather than directly in front, denying him the stun setup. Take W first, hit both strikes on him whenever he steps up to last-hit, and accept that you are building Frost stacks for a level-2 trade rather than killing anyone right now. edits.after: With your level-3 combo reliable and Frost Armor restoring armour and magic resist between trades, you own this lane outright. Track Abyssal Dive — his W is his only escape from your Q initiation and it is 21 seconds at rank 1; when it is down, step to mid-range and force the issue with Arctic Assault. At level 6, Glacial Prison extends your kill threat to 1300 range, so you open with the bola, land the stun, watch Abyssal Dive get panic-burned as an escape rather than a reposition, and follow with Q-W-E while the storm holds him. He cannot Devour an ally to interrupt this chain in a solo-queue 1v1, so the pattern stays clean and repeatable every time the cooldown comes back around.

edits.after: Two items in you are a near-unkillable blizzard machine and Tahm Kench can only survive what you throw, not reverse it — An Acquired Taste adds damage off his own health and ticks far too slowly against your resistances and Sunfire, though three stacks do let him Devour you outright, so never let him free-stack. In teamfights he will Devour an ally to deny your Glacial Prison target; aim the bola at a squishy beside him so his R hands you a free engage instead of eating your CC. Bring Grievous Wounds for his Tongue Lash healing, since an un-shredded Kench simply regenerates the whole exchange. The one genuine threat is him roaming with Abyssal Dive into a side lane — shove the wave so he loses plates every time he leaves.
